scope: Refresh and explicit batch deletion of collection backup snapshots
behavior: Refresh button and activation reread the filesystem and retain existing browsed folders.
Missing folders disappear; incomplete backup sets remain visible with an explicit label.
Ctrl/Shift selection, exact selected-row preview, and a separate permanent-deletion review.
Review includes every path, creation time, operation, and combined file size; Cancel is default.
Only known flat snapshot files are removable; unknown files, reparse paths, nested directories, readonly or locked files are refused.
The entire selected set is planned and locked before mutation; exact object identities and inventory are rechecked.
Deletion uses the original held handles, never recursive path-based removal.
No eager catalog/network load was introduced in startup.
coverage: Refresh after external removal, completed and unfinished backups, multiselection and caret mismatch.
Real confirmation form: both selected full paths, default Cancel, cancellation preserves both snapshots.
Real worker deletes exactly the two confirmed synthetic snapshots and preserves unselected data.
Batch validation, identity/rename checks, inventory mutation, locked files, foreign personal file and junction refusal.
Both themes and 96/144/192 DPI including minimum dialog width.
Existing feedback529 restore, duplicate preview/apply/rollback, series, reader and sync-export checks.
Deferred-startup regression scenario; suite duration is not cold-start latency.

user_data.note: Old collection backups physically remained here; installation backups previously cleaned on G: were a different set.

limitations: Explicit manual cleanup, no automatic retention policy.
Size is calculated on deletion review, not for every list row.
An OS error after deletion begins can leave a partial set; the dialog reports this and refreshes.
Real user snapshots were only inspected; all deletion tests used owned synthetic fixtures.
Existing optional-components verification main ZIPs predate this change and must be repackaged before publication.
